Lawson''' (born July 15, 2000) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for [[Saski Baskonia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. ==Early life== Lawson grew up in [[Brampton]], Ontario and attended GTA Prep in [[Mississauga]], a basketball academy based out of [[Mississauga Secondary School]] where he was coached by David Cooper. In his grade 12 season, Lawson was named a National Preparatory Association First Team All-Star and led the team to second place in the NPA championships.{{cite news|first=Iain|last=Colpitts|title=Trusting the process has kept basketball star AJ Lawson close to home|url=https://www.bramptonguardian.com/community-story/8566051-trusting-the-process-has-kept-basketball-star-aj-lawson-close-to-home/|work=[[Brampton Guardian]]|date=April 25, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Originally set to graduate in 2019 and ranked 40th in his class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] as well as fourth-best Canadian prospect by ''North Pole Hoops'', Lawson [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] for the class of 2018.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Suleymanov|title=Canada's A.J. Lawson commits to South Carolina|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nba/news/aj-lawson-college-commitment-south-carolina-canada-basketball/a6u5mnzuqsqr176gxyh4zmhz2|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=June 27, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Lawson committed to playing college basketball for [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] over offers from [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]] and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]]. South Carolina head coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]] began recruiting Lawson after a late night workout in Columbia on the trip back from a tournament.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Ramspacher|title='In my mind, we got AJ five years ago.' One man's journey to bring AJ Lawson to USC|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article226576129.html|work=The State|date=February 23, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} ==College career== [[File:A.J. Lawson.jpg|thumb|left|Lawson in February 2019]] Lawson averaged 13.4 points, 4.3 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game in 29 games played and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman team.{{cite web|title=South Carolina basketball: Why AJ Lawson's due for big season|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article236514978.html|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=October 23, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|first=John|last=Whittle|title=Lawson deserves 'a little more respect'|url=https://247sports.com/college/south-carolina/Article/South-Carolina-Gamecocks-basketball-AJ-Lawson-snubbed-preseason-All-SEC-team-137064662/|website=247Sports.com|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He was named the SEC Freshman of the Week on November 19, 2018, after averaging 15.7 points, 6.3 rebounds and 5.3 assists over a three-game stretch against [[Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball|Norfolk State]], [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] and [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]].{{cite web|first=John|last=Del Bianco|title=AJ Lawson earns first SEC weekly award|url=https://247sports.com/college/south-carolina/Article/South-Carolina-mens-basketball-Gamecocks-freshman-AJ-Lawson-SEC-Freshman-of-the-Week--124987009/|website=247Sports.com|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Following the season he initially entered his name into the [[2019 NBA draft]], but decided to withdraw and return to South Carolina for his sophomore season.{{cite web|title=Gamecocks' Lawson Declares For NBA Draft, Eligible To Return|url=https://www.live5news.com/2019/04/17/gamecocks-lawson-declares-nba-draft-eligible-return/|website=Live5News.com|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|title=South Carolina freshman AJ Lawson declares for NBA draft|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/04/17/south-carolina-freshman-aj-lawson-declares-for-nba-draft/39356957/|work=[[USA Today]]|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Lawson was named to the preseason first team All-SEC and to the [[Jerry West Award]] watchlist going into his sophomore year.{{cite web|title=A.J. Lawson named Preseason All-SEC First Team by the coaches|url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/local-sports/gamecocks/101-cef555b6-e04b-4dd1-87f4-d0b33e03287f|website=WLTX.com|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|title=USC's Lawson Named To Jerry West Award Watch List|url=https://www.live5news.com/2019/10/16/uscs-lawson-named-jerry-west-award-watch-list/|website=Live5News.com|date=October 15, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He was also named the 41st-best collegiate basketball player going into the 2019–20 season by [[CBS Sports]] and the 29th-best prospect for the [[2020 NBA draft]] by [[ESPN]].{{cite web|first1=Kyle|last1=Boone|first2=Matt|last2=Norlander|first3=Gary|last3=Parrish|title=Ranking the Top 100 And 1 best players in college basketball entering the 2019–20 season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-the-top-100-and-1-best-players-in-college-basketball-entering-the-2019-20-season/|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 24, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=NBA mock draft: Viewer's guide for our top prospects|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/27998169/nba-mock-draft-viewer-guide-our-top-prospects|work=[[ESPN]]|date=November 4, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Lawson scored a season-high 28 points on November 15, 2019, in a 90–63 win against [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]].{{cite web|title=Lawson leads South Carolina past Cleveland State 90–63|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2019/11/15/lawson-leads-south-carolina-past-cleveland-state-90-63/40623929/|work=[[USA Today]]|agency=Associated Press|date=November 15, 2019|access-date=January 30, 2020}} Lawson led the team during the season in total points with 416 and points per game at 13.4 while also averaging 3.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web|first=John|last=Del Bianco|title=Seventh Woods finishes sit-out season on strong note|url=https://247sports.com/college/south-carolina/Article/South-Carolina-Gamecocks-mens-basketball-transfer-guard-Seventh-Woods--145143385/|website=247Sports.com|date=March 18, 2020|access-date=March 21, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the 2020 NBA draft but did not hire an agent.{{cite news|title=South Carolina guard A.J. Lawson declares for NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29101587/south-carolina-guard-aj-lawson-declares-nba-draft|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=April 26, 2020|accessdate=April 27, 2020}} Lawson decided to withdraw from the draft and return to South Carolina on July 29.{{cite news|title=Leading hoops scorer AJ Lawson returning to South Carolina|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/07/29/leading-hoops-scorer-aj-lawson-returning-to-south-carolina/|work=[[NBC Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=July 29, 2020|access-date=August 2, 2020}} On January 6, 2021, Lawson scored a career-high 30 points in a 78–54 win over [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]].{{cite web|title=Lawson scores 30, leads South Carolina over Texas A&M, 78–54|url=https://gamecocksonline.com/news/2021/1/6/mens-basketball-lawson-scores-30-leads-south-carolina-over-texas-am-78-54.aspx|website=GamecocksOnline.com|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210107052455/https://gamecocksonline.com/news/2021/1/6/mens-basketball-lawson-scores-30-leads-south-carolina-over-texas-am-78-54.aspx|archive-date=January 7, 2021}} As a junior, he averaged 16.6 points, 4.1 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.5 steals per game. He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Second Team. On April 19, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and signed an agent.{{cite web|first=Michael|last=Lananna|title=AJ Lawson makes NBA decision official, ending his Gamecocks career|url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/college/university-of-south-carolina/usc-mens-basketball/article250721674.html|work=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]|date=April 19, 2021|access-date=June 16, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===College Park Skyhawks (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Lawson joined the [[Miami Heat]] and [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Greger|title=Rookie Guard Ditches Heat for Hawks at NBA Summer League|url=https://heavy.com/sports/miami-heat/aj-lawson-atlanta-hawks/|website=Heavy.com|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On September 22, 2021, Lawson signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Johnny Hamilton, A.J. Lawson, Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot and Jahlil Okafor|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-johnny-hamilton-aj-lawson-timothe-luwawu-cabarrot-and-jahlil-okafor|website=NBA.com|date=September 22, 2021|access-date=September 22, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 7.{{cite web|title=Hawks Request Waivers On A.J. Lawson, Sign Daquan Jeffries|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-request-waivers-aj-lawson-sign-daquan-jeffries|website=NBA.com|date=October 7, 2021|access-date=October 7, 2021}} In October 2021, Lawson signed with the [[College Park Skyhawks]]{{cite news|title=College Park Skyhawks fall in preseason scrimmage|url=https://www.news-daily.com/sports/college-park-skyhawks-fall-in-preseason-scrimmage/article_d761010e-39c7-11ec-80d5-cfd35a4dd6f8.html|work=[[Clayton News-Daily]]|date=October 30, 2021|access-date=November 3, 2021}} where he played 26 games and averaged 11.8 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.3 steals per game, while shooting 48.1% from the field.{{cite web|title=Guelph Nighthawks Sign Canadian AJ Lawson|url=https://www.cebl.ca/guelph-nighthawks-sign-canadian-aj-lawson|website=CEBL.com|date=April 26, 2022|access-date=April 27, 2022}} ===Guelph Nighthawks (2022)=== On April 26, 2022, Lawson signed with the [[Guelph Nighthawks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]]. ===Minnesota Timberwolves / Iowa Wolves (2022)=== Lawson joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Dallas Mavericks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612742/mavericks|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 5, 2022}} In five games, he averaged 15.6 points and 6.0 rebounds, while shooting 51.9% from the field.{{cite web|first=Grant|last=Afseth|title=EXCLUSIVE: A.J. Lawson Talks Summer Mavs; How He Earned T-Wolves Contract|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-aj-lawson-minnesota-timberwolves-sign-two-way-contract|website=DallasBasketball.com|date=July 19, 2022|access-date=July 20, 2022}} Later, on July 19, 2022, Lawson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|title=Timberwolves To Sign A.J. Lawson To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/07/timberwolves-to-sign-aj-lawson-to-two-way-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|access-date=July 27, 2022}} On October 15, 2022, Lawson was waived by the Timberwolves.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Waive Three Players|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-three-players-3|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=October 15, 2022}} ===Return to College Park (2022)=== On November 3, 2022, Lawson was named to the opening night roster for the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Roster 2022–23|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} On November 16, Lawson signed another two-way contract with the Timberwolves,{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Stanton|title=Timberwolves Sign A.J. Lawson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-a-j-lawson-to-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2022|access-date=December 10, 2022}} but was waived on December 8.{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Matt Ryan to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-matt-ryan-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2022|access-date=December 10, 2022}} Two days later, he returned to College Park.{{cite web|title=AJ Lawson Returns to College Park Skyhawks|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/aj-lawson-returns-to-college-park-skyhawks|website=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2022|access-date=December 10, 2022}} ===Dallas Mavericks / Texas Legends (2022–2024)=== On December 26, 2022, Lawson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|title=Mavs Waive Tyler Dorsey, Sign A.J. Lawson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-waive-tyler-dorsey-sign-aj-lawson-two-way-contract|website=SI.com|date=December 26, 2022|access-date=December 26, 2022}} It was converted to a standard-contract on March 4, 2024.{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Mavericks signed AJ Lawson to a multi-year contract. Lawson played in 28 games for the Mavericks this season, including a 17-point, seven-rebound performance in a win against San Antonio (12/23/23). Both his 17 points and seven rebounds are career-highs.|number=1764721314688872776|user=MavsPR|date=March 4, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2024}} Lawson reached the [[2024 NBA Finals]] where the Mavericks lost to the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.{{cite web|title=Boston Celtics defeat Dallas Mavericks to win 2024 NBA Finals|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/boston-celtics-beat-dallas-mavericks-2024-nba-finals/|website=CBSNews.com|date=June 17, 2024|access-date=June 17, 2024}} On October 8, he was waived by the Mavericks{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have waived guard AJ Lawson.|number=1843700551466553579|user=MavsPR|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Dallas Mavericks Cut AJ Lawson After Preseason Opener; What’s Next?|url=https://dallasbasketball.com/news/dallas-mavericks-cut-aj-lawson-preseason-opener-what-signing-next|website=DallasBasketball.com|date=October 8, 2024|access-date=October 8, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Mavericks' bold decision to cut A.J. Lawson telegraphs next flurry of moves|url=https://thesmokingcuban.com/dallas-mavericks-bold-decision-cut-aj-lawson-telegraphs-next-flurry-of-moves|website=TheSmokingCuban.com|date=October 9, 2024|access-date=October 10, 2024}} and three days later, he signed another two-way contract.{{cite web|title=Mavericks Sign AJ Lawson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/mavericks-sign-aj-lawson-to-two-way-contract/n-6155720|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 11, 2024|access-date=October 12, 2024}} However, he was waived once again on October 18.{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today they have waived guard AJ Lawson, forward Emanuel Miller and center Jamarion Sharp.|number=1847306706323132821|user=MavsPR|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Doyle|last=Rader|title=Dallas Mavericks Waive AJ Lawson, Emanuel Miller And Jamarion Sharp|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/doylerader/2024/10/18/dallas-mavericks-waive-aj-lawson-emanuel-miller-and-jamarion-sharp/|website=Forbes.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} ===Long Island Nets (2024)=== On October 27, 2024, Lawson signed with the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite tweet|author=Long Island Nets|title=Our official training camp roster 🔥 #StrongIsland 💪|number=1850674269581197342|user=LongIslandNets|date=October 27, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2026)=== On December 11, 2024, Lawson signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN LAWSON TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-lawson-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2024|access-date=December 11, 2024}} On March 10, 2025, Lawson scored a career-high 32 points with 12 rebounds against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |title=Raptors 119-104 Wizards (Mar 10, 2025) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401705498 |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=ESPN |language=en}} He posted 28 points in 36 minutes off the bench against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] two days later, shooting 10-20 from the field and 4-9 from three in a 118-105 victory.{{cite web |title=Lawson, Rhoden and Robinson help Raptors beat 76ers 118-105 for 5th win in 6 games |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/lawson-rhoden-and-robinson-help-raptors-beat-76ers-118-105-for-5th-win-in-6-games/ |website=CBS Sports |date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=March 22, 2025}}{{Cite web |title=Raptors 118-105 76ers (Mar 12, 2025) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401705513 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 22, 2025}} On April 12, Lawson and the Raptors converted his two-way contract into a two-year, non-guaranteed contract.{{cite web|last=Maher|first=Rory|title= Raptors Promote A.J. Lawson To Two-Year Standard Deal|url= https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/04/raptors-promoting-a-j-lawson-to-two-year-standard-deal.html|website=hoopsrumors.com|date=April 12, 2025}} He made 26 appearances (two starts) for Toronto during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.1 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. On October 16, 2025, Lawson was waived by the Raptors.{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Raptors Waive Five Players |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-five-players |access-date=October 23, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} Two days later, he re-signed with the team on a two-way contract.{{Cite web|title=Raptors Sign AJ Lawson to Two-Way Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-sign-aj-lawson-to-two-way-contract-2|access-date=October 24, 2025|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}} On April 11, 2026, the Raptors converted Lawson's contract into a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Raptors Convert Lawson To Standard Contract|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-convert-lawson-to-standard-contract|access-date=April 25, 2026|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}} ===Baskonia (2026–present)=== On July 27, 2026, Lawson signed with [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. ==National team career== Lawson has competed internationally for the [[Canada men's national under-19 basketball team]]. He averaged 14.8 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists per game in the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]] as Canada finished second in the tournament.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=Canadian star A.J. Lawson expected to announce Tuesday|url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/06/23/canadian-star-a-j-lawson-closing-in-on-college-decision-2/|website=ZagsBlog.com|date=June 23, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Lawson posted team highs with 18 points and 12 rebounds in Canada's 113–74 loss to the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] in the tournament final.{{cite web|first=Lori|last=Ewing|title=U.S. blows out Canada to win FIBA Americas U18 title|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/canada-united-states-fiba-u18-final-1.4709730|work=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|agency=[[The Canadian Press]]|date=June 16, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} In the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]], Lawson averaged a team-best 16.7 points with 3.9 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game in seven games as Canada advanced to the quarterfinals.{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Ramspacher|title=How close AJ Lawson came to leaving South Carolina, what he learned from Chris Paul|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article232963192.html|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=July 22, 2019}} He also had the highest scoring performance of the tournament with a 31-point game against Senegal.{{cite web|first=Greg|last=Brzozowski|title=Gamecocks' Lawson shines for Canada in win over Senegal|url=https://www.abccolumbia.com/2019/07/04/gamecocks-lawson-shines-for-canada-in-win-over-senegal/|website=ABCColumbia.com|date=July 4, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Lawson made his debut with [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canada's senior men's national team]] during the first round of the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 Americas Qualifiers]].{{cite web|title=Brampton's A.J.
